root_cause.text: The `sys_futex_requeue()` system call failed to validate that the source and destination futexes had identical flags, allowing mismatched flags to trigger a use-after-free (UaF) vulnerability during requeue operations.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check to `SYSCALL_DEFINE4(futex_requeue)` in `kernel/futex/syscalls.c` to return `-EINVAL` if `futexes[0].w.flags != futexes[1].w.flags`, and the commit message states that it was "possible to create a UaF when sys_futex_requeue() is used with different flags."

intent_record.intent_summary: Enforce identical flags for both futexes in the futex_requeue system call to ensure interface consistency.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check in SYSCALL_DEFINE4(futex_requeue) to compare the flags of the two futexes and return -EINVAL if they do not match.
intent_record.how: It prevents execution of the requeue operation when the source and destination futexes have mismatched flags, ensuring configuration consistency.
